scale.label: 39 µm
scale.note: Campaign characteristic length for the Turing pigment-stripe / ocellus wavelength. Not a caliper measurement on the colony photograph.

scale_contrast.coarser: Star-system / zooid spacing is millimetre-scale and is not the wavenumber selected in this slot.
scale_contrast.this_scale: One unstable Turing band at λ = 38.72 µm. The detail window is 7 wavelengths = 271.04 µm.
scale_contrast.finer: Pigment granules of a few micrometres sit at k >> k_c, where σ(k) < 0.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg (1979): f = γ(a - u + u^2 v), g = γ(b - u^2 v)
equations.dispersion: σ(k) is the larger root of s^2 - tr(J - k^2 D) s + det(J - k^2 D) = 0
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.boundary_conditions: Periodic on a square of side L = 7 λ_c = 271.04 µm.

parameters.note: Chosen for slot 3136. Not the sibling slot 0167 parameter set.

empirical_claims: Turing 1952: a homogeneous steady state that is stable without diffusion can be unstable at a finite k_c when the two morphogens diffuse at different rates.
Schnakenberg 1979 supplies the two-species mass-action kinetics used here.

Kondo & Asai 1995 showed that a reaction-diffusion wavelength can organize vertebrate pigment stripes. That result is not a measurement on Botryllus; it is cited only as the pigment-stripe exemplar of the same law.

Sorrentino, Manni, Lane & Burighel 2000 describe the ascidian larval cerebral vesicle and its sensory organs, including the ocellus, which is the anatomical structure this detail-scale wavelength is aimed at.
Cloney 1982 reviews ascidian larval metamorphosis, including colonial species such as Botryllus.
This slot does not claim that a published micrograph measured an ocellus or pigment repeat of exactly 38.72 µm.
